How do you secure renewable energy assets where industrial control systems, cloud platforms and cybersecurity come together? At OX2, protecting wind, solar and energy storage facilities mean understanding both the technology behind energy production and the risks that come with connected systems. We are now looking for a OT Security Lead to take ownership of our cybersecurity priorities with operational technology at the center and help shape how security is managed across our growing energy portfolio.
YOU WILL
OX2 is a renewable energy company developing, constructing, owning and operating large-scale wind, solar and energy storage projects. As the company expands its role as an independent power producer, cybersecurity is an important part of ensuring that its energy assets and the systems supporting them remain secure and reliable.  As OT Security Lead, you will take overall responsibility for cybersecurity across OX2's IT and operational technology environments, with a clear focus on OT. You will work across industrial control systems, cloud platforms and corporate IT, setting security requirements and ensuring that risks are understood and addressed throughout the development and operation of energy assets.
You will make risk-based decisions about which security measures are needed, where they should be implemented and how they should be prioritized across different facilities. Working closely with plant engineers, IT teams, suppliers and senior stakeholders, you will translate security requirements into practical solutions that work in operational environments.
Your main responsibilities will be to:

Own and prioritize the CSMS pipeline across OX2's wind, solar and energy storage assets.

Define security architecture and requirements across OT and IT, including SCADA, plant control systems, remote sites, Azure, AWS and SaaS environments.

Apply IEC 62443 and security principles such as zones and conduits, secure remote access, least privilege and security by design.

Establish and enforce cybersecurity requirements for suppliers, technology partners and external service providers.

Assess cybersecurity risks in vendor selection, acquisitions and divestments, contributing to cyber due diligence.

Govern external security partners and managed security service providers, including incident response and security delivery.

Translate NIS2 and relevant cybersecurity legislation into practical security measures across the business

The role involves collaboration across OX2's international business.

YOU ARE 
You have a strong background in cybersecurity. You understand the challenges of protecting systems where security, availability and operational requirements need to work together. You have worked with OT and industrial control systems, including areas such as SCADA, plant networks and remote access. You have practical experience with IEC 62443 and understand how to apply security principles such as network segmentation, zones and conduits, least privilege and security by design. You also understand the connections between OT, corporate IT and cloud environments.
Your experience extends beyond individual projects. You have taken responsibility for security across multiple sites or technical environments, setting priorities, assessing risks and ensuring that security measures are implemented. You are used to working with external suppliers and know how to establish requirements and challenge solutions. Experience with MSSP governance, incident response or cyber due diligence is particularly valuable.
You are naturally curious and enjoy exploring new technologies and approaches to security. You make well-founded decisions. You can discuss technical details with engineers while explaining risks and priorities clearly to management. Most importantly, you follow through and make sure security requirements lead to real improvements. You have a relevant educational background and are fluent in English. Experience from energy, utilities, industrial automation or other critical infrastructure environments is particularly valuable, but not essential if you bring strong practical OT security experience.
At OX2, you will have the opportunity to influence how cybersecurity is managed across an international portfolio of renewable energy assets. You will work close to the technology behind energy production, with the responsibility and autonomy to develop security capabilities that protect both current operations and future assets.
WANT TO KNOW MORE? 
For questions about the role, please contact recruitment consultant Johanna Värmfors at johanna.varmfors@nexergroup.com or +46 730 821 230, or Artan Bitiqi at artan.bitiqi@nexergroup.com or +46 723 61 28 44.
We are looking forward hearing from you!
ABOUT OX2
OX2 is a renewable energy company accelerating the transition to a sustainable energy system. Through its integrated model as an independent power producer (IPP), OX2 develops, constructs, owns and manages renewable energy assets across onshore and offshore wind, solar and energy storage.  With a diversified portfolio of approximately 33 GW across development, construction, asset management and operations, OX2 combines entrepreneurial project development with long-term ownership and value creation. The company operates in five European markets and Australia, has approximately 500 employees, and is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden.  OX2 is owned by EQT, one of the world's largest private equity investors.

Utility is entering an exciting new chapter.
After being part of the Svea Solar Group, we are now an independent company with secured financing of up to EUR 185 million. Our ambition is to expand our operating portfolio of solar PV assets and Battery Energy Storage Systems to more than 2 GW over the next five years, roughly equivalent to the capacity of two large nuclear reactors.
For our Finance team, that means growth, new legal entities and plenty of opportunities to build and improve how we work.

Utility consists of 35 colleagues, and the team is a big part of why she enjoys coming to work. There is trust and a strong sense of collaboration. You own your work, while having colleagues around you who are always willing to help and share their knowledge.

Be part of various projects to identify improvements in processes and systems, for example exploring how AI can improve efficiency.

Requirements

Experience working with Swedish GAAP K3.

Thorough understanding of financial regulations, accounting principles and reporting standards.

Experience developing and implementing new routines and processes.

Proficient in business communication in both English and Swedish.

Valuable experience, but not required:

Experience working in a balance-sheet-heavy business.

Experience with consolidation and operating in a multi-legal-entity environment with many intercompany flows.

Experience working in Cognos.

Personal qualities
Own It: Takes initiative to drive improvements and moves processes forward with a solution-oriented mindset.
Accuracy: Works systematically and delivers high-quality work across a high volume of accounting tasks, while staying organised and meeting deadlines.
Create Good Vibes & Do It Together: Contributes to a positive team environment by bringing energy, supporting colleagues and sharing knowledge. Gives both positive and constructive feedback in a respectful and encouraging way.
What we offer you
Make a big impact in a growing company. We’re still a relatively lean organisation, which means your ideas, decisions and initiatives can have a real impact on how we grow and work.

Be part of the energy transition at scale. Contribute to a cleaner energy future through large-scale solar parks and innovative energy solutions.

Stable benefits, and the best benefit of all: the people. 30 days of vacation, occupational pension, healthcare allowance, parking, the option to work from home up to two days a week, regular after works and, most importantly, an engaged and inclusive team.

About us
Svea Solar Utility (“SSU”) is a leading Swedish solar IPP with currently 8 solar parks in operation, totaling 75 MWp, 2 parks under construction, totaling 125 MWp, and a development pipeline of over 3 GW across more than 100 projects.
SSU was, until May 2026, an independently managed subsidiary of Svea Renewable Solar AB (“Svea Group”), but is now majority-owned directly by Altor, a leading Swedish Private Equity firm. The full separation from Svea Group is ongoing, and as part of the process, SSU will be rebranded during autumn 2026. Read our press release here.

Job Description
WHAT YOU’LL DO
As a Sales Advisor at H&M, you’ll play a key role in creating an outstanding customer experience. You’ll welcome customers, guide them through your store, and support them in finding what they need while showcasing our products. Acting in line with our values, you’ll contribute to both your own success and the success of the company.
You will:

Collaborate with your team to deliver exceptional service at every step of the customer journey.

Represent yourself and the brand positively during all customer interactions.

As part of the dynamic Store Team, every role—from Sales Advisors, Department Managers, Store Managers and Visual Merchandisers to Assistant Store Managers, Cash Office Responsible, and Delivery Responsible in larger stores—contributes to creating an inspiring and welcoming environment. You’ll also connect with the wider Area Team, collaborating across stores to share insights and drive success together. By building meaningful connections with customers in our stores, we make fashion accessible and sustainable for all.

We are looking for people with…
Experience in customer service within fashion, retail, or similar fields.

And people who are…
Passionate about fashion and delivering an exceptional in-store experience while promoting our products and driving sales.
Thriving in collaborative and dynamic environments.
Communicative, creative, curious to work with store technology, with a strong eagerness to learn and develop.
Flexible and action oriented.

H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future.

 All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online.

About Taigatech
We solve some of the most important problems in industry with AI and computer vision. With our connection to the latest research and academia, we take world-leading research in AI and computer vision and turn it into impactful solutions that help the wood industry increase yield, availability, and productivity.
Technology is reshaping our world. We believe the forest and wood products have an important role to play in a sustainable future, and AI is how the industry gets there.
We are a growing team in a comfortable office in central Gothenburg, working closely with many of the leading names in wood processing. Our systems run in production at sawmills and pulp mills in Sweden and abroad. There's no better time to join our journey than now.
Why this role exists
Our systems create value the moment their output reaches the customer's control system — a correction, a signal, something the line can act on.
What determines the results are a handful of decisions made early and made well: which signal, where it lands, what the line does with it, and how it behaves when something unexpected happens. Get those right and the implementation is small and quick.
Today that judgement is distributed between our own team and the automation partners we work with on each installation. We want someone to decide what the interface should look like, judge whether it came out right, decide when a sensor or other component needs replacing, and if the signal belongs on a different fieldbus.
That's the person we're hiring. You don't replace our automation partners. You become the one who leads them.
What you'll do
The role is both technical and leadership, and the balance shifts from project to project.
Own the machine-side interface. You decide how our system talks to the customer's PLC. Signals, timing, handshakes, watchdog, fail-safe behaviour. You write the functional description the work is built from.
Lead our automation partners. Sometimes that means writing the code snippet yourself. Sometimes it means explaining what needs doing and reviewing that it came out right. You decide which.
Make the technical decisions on the customer's plant. Upgrading a component for better results, or moving to a different fieldbus, is yours to propose and drive. The implementation itself normally goes to a partner.
Be the customer's main contact through the project — scope, timeline, status, time and cost reporting. You take over from sales and carry the delivery home.
Clear the path. OT network access, change control, and the dialogue with the site's automation and IT departments, so the installation can be done quickly and safely.
Work closely with our ML and vision engineers. Translate what the process needs into what the model has to output, and the model's limits back into what we can promise.
Make it repeatable. A reusable interface specification, a commissioning checklist, and a growing network of automation partners to deliver alongside.
Who you are
You need experience, but we don't care how many years you have behind you. We care about what you've done.
You have programmed PLCs in live production, on at least one major platform — Siemens TIA/S7, Beckhoff, ABB, Mitsubishi, Codesys or equivalent
You have hands-on experience of industrial networks: Profinet, Profibus, EtherCAT, Modbus TCP, OPC UA or equivalent.
You have extended control systems you did not write with retrofits onto existing, running equipment
You have written functional descriptions that someone else built from
You have stood on site during commissioning, with production running and someone waiting
Drives the project forward by keeping people accountable, asking the right questions, and pushing decisions when it matters — even when that means a difficult conversation.
Swedish and English, and you sometimes travel to sites
Bonus
Sawmill, pulp and paper, or other heavy process industry
Vision systems, sensors or measurement equipment
Experience on the supplier side, responsible for subcontractors
Machinery directive and risk assessment on modified lines
Python and basic data analysis
What we offer
You'll be our first dedicated automation hire. You set the delivery process, and it becomes the standard we scale on. As delivery volume grows, the function gets built around you.
You'll work directly with the founders, with our ML engineers and with the mills themselves. Office in Gothenburg.
We review applications on a rolling basis.
Öppen för alla
Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.

Experience with Java application server frameworks, such as JBoss and Tomcat.

Experience working with Microsoft SQL Server and T-SQL.

Understanding of networking concepts, including firewalls and load balancing.

Overall areas of responsibilities and activities

A Vision Automation Engineer in a cell manufacturing company plays a key role in developing, optimizing, reverse-engineering, and maintaining machine vision and optical inspection systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. They are responsible for programming, troubleshooting, and improving cameras, lighting configurations, and image processing algorithms, supporting both legacy production line re-commissioning and new vision system installations. The role also includes ensuring accurate data transfer, system connectivity, and smooth communication with PLCs, SCADA, and upper-level MES platforms to enable inline defect traceability, dimensional inspection, and digital integration. Close collaboration with production, engineering, and maintenance teams is required to identify and implement solutions that improve quality, throughput, and equipment uptime. A strong focus is placed on continuous improvement, safety, and scalability to meet the growing demand for electric vehicle battery production. 

Key Responsibilities 
Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to) 
Participate in HAZOP sessions and ensure compliance with process safety, operational safety, and environmental standards relating to equipment control and programming.  
Responsible for the FATs of the equipment (Project timeline dependent).  
Lead vision system integration and optical calibration during equipment commissioning and line re-starts (Project timeline dependent). 
Develop and reverse-engineer the vision inspection systems to be implemented in the production and logistics equipment in the factory, as well as the relevant specifications and documentation. 
Author and review engineering design documentation (Specifications, Functional design, Logic diagrams, Test Cases, Test Records).  
Train and mentor new engineers, and educate other support functions on machine vision, optics, and quality inspection gates. 
Code review and test of suppliers' vision software and algorithmic work within the projects to validate specified defect detection thresholds (Gauge R&R) and to ensure the quality and reliability of the data transferred from the equipment to the upper-level systems. 
Participate in R&D activities for piloting of new technologies and their suitability to production environments. 
Define and improve the factory blueprint, general specifications and ways of working in collaboration with the extended automation and digitalization teams. (Project timeline dependent). 
Contribute to technical improvements, development and optimization of software processes internally in the automation team 
The role requires regular presence on the production floor, with a minimum of approximately 25% of working hours spent on-site. Depending on project needs (such as line re-commissioning), there may be periods where up to 100% of working hours are required on the shop floor. 
Develop and maintain machine vision and image processing programming standards. 
Guide and mentor colleagues to industrial best practices, focussing on growth and development. 
Complete supplementary tasks as seen fit by management to effectively utilize time and resource for the benefit of the business. 

Requirements 
Educational background and previous experience required for the role 

Qualifications and Experience 
Bachelors Degree in Electronics, Mechatronics, Electrical, Automation, Robotics, Software Engineering or similar. 
Minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience within Industrial Automation in process-driven or discrete manufacturing industries such as: Battery Cell, Automotive, Chemical, Paper, Semiconductors, Pharma, Food, Warehouses, etc. 
Experience of working with industrial camera systems, optical components, and lighting techniques, including the selection, configuration, and calibration of camera hardware for manufacturing inspection and process control applications 
Experience in the design, configuration, and deployment of machine vision systems including cameras, lighting, and vision software platforms such as Cognex, Halcon, or equivalent, with experience integrating vision outputs into PLC, SCADA, and MES environments via OPC connectivity. 
Experience developing and optimising image processing pipelines and vision algorithms for applications such as defect detection, pattern recognition, and dimensional verification, with familiarity with industrial communication protocols for vision system integration. 
Experience in writing technical documentation including inspection requirement specifications, algorithm validation reports, vision system configuration records, functional design, UML, test cases, and test records. 
Experience with image processing software and programming tools relevant to industrial vision applications, such as Python, C++, OpenCV, or equivalent vision libraries, with the ability to develop, test, and optimise vision algorithms for real-time manufacturing environments 
Experienced continuous improvement and root cause analysis. 

Specific skills 
Strong knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems. 
Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices for manufacturing systems. 
Troubleshooting skills with diagnostic equipment. 
Ability to document technical problems concisely. 
Excellent English skills, both written and oral, are essential. Basic Swedish and other language skills are a plus. You should have good communication skills and be able to work in close collaboration with colleagues from many different teams. 
Ability to work within varying environments including clean-rooms and dry-rooms, while wearing appropriate PPE. 
Comfortable operating in high-profile, international, and high-pressure environments. 
A genuine technical interest and passion about working within production is highly valued.

Design and support integrations between MES, SAP S/4HANA, production equipment, and other business-critical systems.

5+ years of experience working with MES solutions in manufacturing environments, preferably within highly automated production facilities.

Experience with C#, T-SQL, Microsoft SQL Server, relational databases, and industrial communication standards such as OPC UA.

Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Fluency in Swedish and English.

Experience working in Agile development environments.

Nobia is Europe’s leading kitchen specialist and part of everyday life for millions of people, with the kitchen playing an increasingly important role in modern homes. The Group consists of eighteen strong brands, including Marbodal, HTH, Sigdal, and uno form.

jobs.description:
Mälardalen University (MDU) is the youngest university in Sweden. In line with our vision, to be a progressive and collaborative University where we shape a sustainable future together, we wish to make a difference.Do you want to be involved and contribute to our development?Together, we can create a sustainable future through knowledge and innovation. We believe that knowledge and new perspectives are best attained and reached together in collaboration with others – our colleagues, students, the private and public sectors, both nationally and internationally.The Faculty of Engineering and Health Sciences provides education and conducts research in engineering, health and information design, with a clear focus on addressing societal challenges. Our research is carried out in close collaboration with external partners, both nationally and internationally, and contributes to knowledge development and innovation. Through our collaboration platforms, we bring together academia, the public sector and industry to jointly drive knowledge development and strengthen the relevance of research and education. Education at all levels is research-based and closely aligned with the needs of society and working life. Together, we contribute to sustainable societal development.The Faculty comprises three departments with a total of approximately 500 staff.The Department of Computer Science and Engineering conducts internationally recognised research in close collaboration with industry, the public sector and other higher education institutions, in areas including artificial intelligence, dependable systems, embedded systems, and medical and health technologies. The department educates students in fields such as computer science, software engineering, computer networks, applied AI, dependable systems, cybersecurity, and intelligent embedded systems.
Employment information
 
Employment: Temporary employment, 2 years
 
Period of employment/Start date: March 2027 or as soon as possible
 
Scope: Full time
 
Number of positions: 1
 
Closing date for application: 2026-12-31
 
Campus location: Västerås
 
School: Datavetenskap och datateknik
Position description
The purpose of the position is to give the employee an early opportunity to develop his or her independence as a researcher and to create the conditions for further acquisitions of qualifications after completing the doctoral degree. The position is a temporary employment with a maximum period of 3 years. 
As postdoc in the Chips-JU uPQComing project, the candidate is expected to lead their line of research, both individually and in collaboration with other project members, both at MDU and in the consortium. The tasks involved in the employment include also co-supervision of PhD students, project meetings, participation and presentation at research venues as well as project reporting events. The postdoc is expected to teach for 10% of their employment time.
Qualification requirements
The applicant is required to have a PhD in Physics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering or Quantum Computing
The applicant must have completed the degree no more than three years before the end of the application period. You have not previously held a position as a postdoctoral researcher in the same or related subject area at MDU that exceeds one year.
Documented research in quantum computing is required. The candidate shall demonstrate advanced skills in conducting both research and implementation tasks (e.g. first-/single-author publications, own GitHub repository, etc.). Written and oral communication skills: demonstrates the ability to communicate ideas clearly and persuasively, both in writing and orally. This includes the ability to articulate complex concepts in accessible language during one-to-one meetings and presentations to both small and large groups. Requirements for employment are the ability to teach and conduct research in English.
This position involves work within a research project where access to certain research results, methods, technical systems, software or other information may be regulated by export control, security or sanctions legislation. The successful candidate must therefore be able to meet the requirements set out in the relevant legislation in order to gain access to the project’s research environment and to be able to carry out the duties of the position. A security clearance or other legally justified checks may be carried out if the nature of the position requires so.  
Assessment criteria
For this position, particular emphasis will be placed on: 
Documented knowledge and research in (post-)quantum cryptography and/or cybersecurity is considered a merit
Knowledge of digital-twins is considered a merit
Documented collaborations with researchers outside their own supervision team and/or with industry are considered a merit
